mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) above 2% annualized over the past two months signals inflationary pressure, leading to tighter monetary policy expectations and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns of S&P 500 are positive in more than 60% of the instances where CPIAUCSL annualized increase exceeds 2%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) over the past two months indicates a strengthening economy, which boosts consumer confidence and spending, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns of S&P 500 are negative in more than 40% of the instances where HOUST increases by more than 5% over two months.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 5% signals a tightening labor market, which can lead to wage inflation and increased corporate costs, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns of S&P 500 are positive in more than 50% of the instances where UNRATE falls below 5%.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% over the past two months indicates increased economic activity, which is generally positive for corporate earnings and thus leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 5-day forward returns of S&P 500 are negative in more than 60% of the instances where INDPRO increases by more than 1% over two months.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) signals an easing monetary policy, which typically leads to increased liquidity in the market and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns of S&P 500 are negative in more than 40% of the instances following a decrease in FEDFUNDS.

mechanism_narrative: When real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) increase by more than 1% month-over-month and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) decreases, it signals a strengthening consumer economy, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS increase > 1% MoM and UNRATE decrease
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns of S&P 500 are negative in more than 50% of the instances where RSAFS increases by more than 1% MoM and UNRATE decreases.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) by more than 200,000 over the past month signals a strong labor market, which is generally positive for economic growth and thus leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns of S&P 500 are negative in more than 40% of the instances where PAYEMS increases by more than 200,000 in a month.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 4% and the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) is increasing, it indicates a tightening monetary policy in response to inflation, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns of S&P 500 are positive in more than 50% of the instances where FEDFUNDS is above 4% and CPIAUCSL is increasing.
